metadata.title: Kaelon Black Worth Stashing Off the Waiver Wire Through Week 8 Bye
metadata.description: San Francisco 49ers rookie running back Kaelon Black had the best game of his young career in Week 7, recording 12 carries for 63 yards and a touchdown in his team's loss to the Atlanta Falcons. Black's fantasy upside is limited by the presence of star 49ers back Christian McCaffrey (thigh). Still, Black has seen relatively consistent work in a secondary role this season, recording 57 carries for 223 yards and a touchdown across seven games. McCaffrey also suffered a thigh injury in Week 7. Both he and the team have downplayed the injury, and the 49ers have their bye in Week 8, so McCaffrey may not miss any time. However, even a small increase in Black's touches coming out of the bye could put him in flex range for fantasy managers in the right matchups. Of course, if McCaffrey were to be sidelined for any reason, Black would be a must-start running back. Black should be rostered across almost all fantasy formats coming out of Week 7.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black - Efficient with expanded opportunity
metadata.description: Black rushed 12 times for 63 yards and a touchdown and brought in one of three targets for minus-4 yards in the 49ers' 29-20 loss to the Falcons on Sunday. He also lost a fumble and returned one kickoff for 34 yards.
metadata.analysis: Christian McCaffrey suffered a thigh injury in the opening period that eventually led to him missing the entire second quarter, affording Black expanded opportunity. The rookie made good use of the extra touches, averaging a career-high 5.3 yards per carry and recording his highest rushing yardage total since his Week 1 NFL debut. Black also rang up his first TD as a professional, a 30-yard breakaway run on the first play of the second quarter. However, the rookie made a key mistake when he lost a fumble with San Francisco nearing the red zone in the second quarter. McCaffrey did return to the game for the second half and now has the Week 8 bye to recover, so Black could be back to a more reduced role in a Week 9 home matchup against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 8.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black finds the end zone in Week 7 loss
metadata.description: Kaelon Black rushed for 63 yards and a touchdown on 12 carries in Sunday's 29-20 loss to the Falcons.
metadata.analysis: Black led the 49ers in carries Sunday afternoon and gashed the Falcons' defense for a 30-yard TD run in the second quarter. Christian McCaffrey did deal with a thigh issue in this one and ended up only outtouching Black 13-to-12. This was a nice game for Black, but he remains useful to fantasy managers only as a handcuff to McCaffrey.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black Sees Increased Opportunity in Loss
metadata.description: San Francisco 49ers running back Kaelon Black struggled early on during Sunday's game, but he was able to turn it around. Black was stopped on three straight plays inside the three-yard line on the first drive of the game. He was pretty quiet in this game until Christian McCaffrey (thigh) was forced to exit during the first half. Black took over the lead back role for a period of time and posted some decent numbers. Overall, Black carried the ball 12 times for 63 yards and a touchdown in the loss to the Atlanta Falcons. McCaffrey returned in the second half of this game, so he should be fine moving forward. Black remains one of the better handcuffs heading into the team's Week 8 bye.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black a Top Handcuff to Roster in Fantasy Football
metadata.description: San Francisco 49ers running back Kaelon Black currently lacks standalone value in his role as the No. 2 ball-carrier behind Christian McCaffrey. However, he is one of the league's highest-upside handcuffs because of how much his value would rise if McCaffrey were to miss any time. McCaffrey had 25 touches last week, including nine receptions. While Black may not quite handle that many touches in this hypothetical jump to the No. 1 spot on the depth chart, he would absolutely be the lead-back option ahead of Jordan James, who hasn't played an offensive snap since Week 2. Black has been much more involved to this point, amassing 45 carries, 170 rushing yards, two catches, and eight receiving yards. Evidently, while Black would take on a lot of McCaffrey's hypothetically vacated rushing attempts, the 25-year-old rookie doesn't have much appeal in the passing game, and so he'd have less value and a lower floor in PPR leagues compared to half-PPR and standard formats.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black Likely to See Limited Workload in Week 7
metadata.description: Across six games in 2026, San Francisco 49ers rookie running back Kaelon Black has recorded 45 carries for 170 yards and two catches for eight yards on three targets. While Black has seen at least six carries in all but one of the 49ers' games this season, his production upside is capped by the presence of star San Francisco back Christian McCaffrey. In Week 7, the 49ers will take on the Atlanta Falcons. Atlanta has fielded a strong run defense in 2026, ranking sixth in the NFL in both yards per carry allowed (3.6) and total rushing yards allowed (499). Black remains a priority handcuff running back option for fantasy managers to stash in a bench spot. However, with McCaffrey entering the game fully healthy, Black is hard to trust as a starter in Week 7.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black Remains a High-Upside Waiver-Wire Handcuff
metadata.description: San Francisco 49ers rookie running back Kaelon Black remains a high-upside handcuff after rushing eight times for 34 yards in Monday's win over Washington. Black handled 26.8% of the team's rushing attempts, up from his 21.1% average share during Weeks 2-5. Christian McCaffrey remains the clear lead back, limiting Black's immediate fantasy value. However, the rookie has established himself as San Francisco's primary backup and could inherit a substantial workload if McCaffrey misses time. Black is rostered in just 28% of Yahoo leagues, making him an appealing stash for fantasy managers seeking high-upside running back insurance.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black sees nine touches in MNF win
metadata.description: Kaelon Black carried the ball eight times for 34 yards while catching his lone target for a three-yard gain in a 23-17 win over the Commanders in Week 6's Monday night game.
metadata.analysis: Black looked good playing behind Christian McCaffrey, averaging 4.3 yards per carry for the 49ers. The rookie remains one of the top handcuffs in fantasy heading into a Week 7 matchup vs. the Falcons.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black - Nine touches in Week 6 win
metadata.description: Black rushed eight times for 34 yards and brought in his only target for three yards in the 49ers' 23-17 win over the Commanders on Monday night.
metadata.analysis: Black logged half as many carries as Christian McCaffrey and a whopping nine fewer targets, cementing the pecking order in the 49ers' ground attack. However, Black is getting some nice complementary run as a rookie, as he's logged 45 carries over his first six games. Black has just three targets in that same span, however, so his fantasy upside will remain capped to a large degree in a Week 7 road matchup against the Falcons on Sunday.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black - Misses practice Saturday, will play Monday
metadata.description: Black was excused from Saturday's practice to address a personal matter but does not have an injury designation for Monday's Week 6 matchup against Washington, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Since Black wasn't given an injury designation, his absence from practice Saturday isn't expected to impact his availability Monday. The rookie should thus continue to work as the 49ers' No.2 running back behind Christian McCaffrey. That role hasn't yielded much fruit for Black of late, however, as he's totaled fewer than 20 yards in each of his past three contests.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black Could See More Work In Mismatch
metadata.description: San Francisco 49ers running back Kaelon Black hasn't seen much work as the team's change-of-pace back lately. The rookie wowed in Week 1, handing a season-high 14 carries for 65 yards, but he has averaged 5.8 carries and 17.8 rushing yards in the four games since. The disparity between the 49ers and Commanders in their Week 6 meeting could put more on Black's plate. If the 49ers get out to an early lead, they are more likely to preserve Christian McCaffrey and give more work to Black, as we saw in Week 1. The Commanders' run defense has been stout, allowing the sixth-fewest rushing yards to running backs, but the 49ers' improved run blocking in 2026 has led to 4.6 yards per attempt. Black projects as an RB4/5 in Week 6. While he won't be suitable to start in most leagues, his upside makes him an option in deep leagues that may need a solution as a bye-week streamer.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black Potentially in Line for an Expanded Role
metadata.description: As injuries continue to mount for the San Francisco 49ers, rookie running back Kaelon Black could soon be tasked with handling a heavier workload, adding modest flex appeal to his potentially week-winning insurance value. Wide receiver Deebo Samuel Sr. (hamstring), who has carried the ball nine times on the year, is the latest Niners player to succumb to injury, now expected to miss a handful of games with a hamstring injury. Through five weeks, Black has handled a 36.2% running back rush share, but with San Francisco's receiver room stretched so thin by injury, there is added potential for Black and Christian McCaffrey to share the field more frequently, with the latter split out wide. With four NFL teams on bye in Week 6, Black becomes a desperation flex option in deeper leagues and needs to be rostered in all formats.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black sees six carries Sunday
metadata.description: Kaelon Black ran for 16 yards on six carries in the 49ers 32-29 win over the Seahawks.
metadata.analysis: Black remains a pure stash for fantasy managers.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black Best Left On Bench In Week 5
metadata.description: San Francisco 49ers running back Kaelon Black (illness) showed promise as Christian McCaffrey's understudy in Week 1. In the season opener, the rookie handled 14 carries for 65 yards. His effectiveness seemed to open the door to a rotation to keep McCaffrey fresh, but Black has not seen more than seven carries in a game over the last three weeks. Black was limited in practice earlier this week by an illness, but he was a full participant on Thursday and Friday and has no designation for the 49ers' upcoming game against the Seahawks. Deep-league fantasy managers who are keeping weekly tabs on Black as an option should wait another week. Seattle is allowing the lowest rushing success rate and fourth-lowest EPA per rushing attempt. Black's opportunities to get on the field may also be limited in what is expected to be a hotly contested divisional matchup. Black is projected as an RB5 and should remain a bench stash for the time being.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black (illness) off injury report Sunday
metadata.description: Kaelon Black is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
metadata.analysis: Black will remain a change-of-pace role alongside Christian McCaffrey.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black Continues Seeing Reduced Role
metadata.description: San Francisco 49ers running back Kaelon Black got his career started great with 65 rushing yards on 14 attempts during the season opener. Since then, Black has carried the ball 17 times for 55 yards over the last three games. The rookie back has certainly taken a step back over the last few weeks. Fantasy managers were hopeful that Black would remain a 10-plus carry player every week, but that was unlikely to happen with Christian McCaffrey healthy right now. Black is still one of the better handcuffs to roster given McCaffrey's injury history. The 24-year-old isn't someone that should be started in fantasy formats given his recent struggles ahead of the Week 5 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black (illness) upgraded to full participant Thursday
metadata.description: Kaelon Black (illness) was upgraded to a full participant at practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Black was limited by an illness on Wednesday, but he's over it at this point and was able to practice in full on Thursday. He should be good to go for Week 5 and will continue to be San Francisco's RB2 for as long as he remains healthy and on the field.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black - Back to full practice Thursday
metadata.description: Black (illness) upgraded to a full practice Thursday, Harrison Rich of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
metadata.analysis: Black was limited Wednesday but appears to be fine ahead of Sunday's Week 5 date with the Seahawks. The rookie running back has plodded to 2.5 yards per carry over the last three weeks and is merely a bench stash in fantasy as Christian McCaffrey's top backup.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black - Limited by illness Wednesday
metadata.description: Black (illness) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Cam Inman of The San Jose Mercury News reports.
metadata.analysis: Black should be fine to handle his normal role Sunday against the Seahawks as Christian McCaffrey's direct backup. The rookie running back has turned 20 carries into just 55 yards (2.75 YPC) over the last three games following a strong Week 1 debut in Australia against the Rams.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black (illness) limited in practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Kaelon Black is limited in practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Black is dealing with an illness. He should still be good to go on Sunday against the Seahawks.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black - Inefficient in Week 4 win
metadata.description: Black turned six carries into 13 yards during the 49ers' 24-14 win over the Broncos on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Black's longest carry of the day went for five yards, with four of his other touches going for two yards or fewer. With Christian McCaffrey clearly leading the backfield, Black's workload will be volatile on a week-to-week basis and dependant on game script. The 49ers will hit the road for Week 5 in an NFC West showdown against the 3-1 Seahawks.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black sees six carries in win Sunday
metadata.description: Kaelon Black rushed six times for 13 yards in Sunday's 24-14 win over the Denver Broncos.
metadata.analysis: Black saw some work behind Christian McCaffrey but wasn't able to do much with it, averaging just 2.2 yards per carry. He remains a lottery ticket in San Francisco's backfield and doesn't have standalone fantasy value as long as McCaffrey is healthy.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black Remains an Appealing Running Back Stash on the Waiver Wire
metadata.description: Across the first four games of his NFL career, San Francisco 49ers rookie running back Kaelon Black has recorded 31 carries for 120 yards. Black's production upside in San Francisco is firmly capped by the presence of superstar 49ers back Christian McCaffrey. As long as McCaffrey remains healthy, Black is highly unlikely to provide fantasy managers with consistent production. However, Black has clearly established himself as San Francisco's RB2. McCaffrey is in his age-30 season, has a history of significant injuries, and is coming off an NFL-leading 413 touches in 2025. If McCaffrey were to get injured, Black could immediately vault into must-start running back status as the lead back in the potent 49ers offense. In fantasy leagues with 12 or more teams, Black remains a worthy waiver wire target.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black's Playing Time At Risk
metadata.description: San Francisco 49ers running back Kaelon Black saw a healthy 38.5% snap share in the first two games of the season. The 49ers had both contests well in hand early on, allowing them to get Black involved frequently as a means of managing Christian McCaffrey's workload. When the Cardinals proved surprisingly pesky in Week 3, San Francisco leaned on their star at the expense of the rookie, who saw just eight snaps to CMC's 45. That pattern may follow in Week 4, when the 49ers take on the Denver Broncos, who have engineered fourth-quarter comebacks in each of the last two weeks. On the plus side, the Broncos have been soft against the run so far in 2026, giving up the third-highest yards per carry and highest EPA per rush attempt. Black is projected as a borderline RB4/5 for Week 4. Fantasy managers may want to look for an option with more certain playing time before plugging Black into their lineups.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black - Sees workload dip vs. Arizona
metadata.description: Black turned four carries into 17 yards and failed to haul in his lone target during the 49ers' 36-30 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Black accumulated 95 scrimmage yards on 22 touches through the first two games of the regular season and was a regular rotational piece in the offense behind Christian McCaffrey. However, Black observed most of Sunday's game from the sidelines, seeing the field for only eight of the 49ers' 54 offensive snaps (14.8 percent) compared to McCaffrey's 45 snaps. Keeping McCaffrey healthy is a top priority for the 49ers, so Black figures to see more playing time moving forward in order to preserve the former's workload. The 49ers will remain home for Week 4 to host the Broncos this Sunday.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black Still a Valuable Insurance Back Despite Dwindling Usage
metadata.description: San Francisco 49ers running back Kaelon Black has seen his involvement dwindle week over week, but he remains one of the most valuable insurance backs in the league. After carrying the ball 14 times in the season opener, Black has logged only 11 carries over the past two outings, and he's a player to look out for as a potential post-waiver pickup. With injuries mounting and bye weeks approaching, Black could be dropped by managers facing a roster crunch, and while he may not have the standalone value implied by his Week 1 usage, he is still worthy of an end-of-bench spot. Over three games, he has racked up 107 rushing yards on his 25 carries, and he has weekly RB1 potential if All-Pro Christian McCaffrey were to miss time.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black quiet Sunday
metadata.description: Kaelon Black ran for 17 yards on four carries in the 49ers 36-30 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Black saw one target which he didn't haul in. Christian McCaffrey took over as the clear lead back on the afternoon. Black remains a stash for fantasy managers.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black Could Get More Opportunities in Week 3 vs. Cardinals
metadata.description: San Francisco 49ers running back Kaelon Black could be a sneaky fantasy asset in Week 3 against the visiting Arizona Cardinals. The rookie back is still looking for his first regular-season touchdown but has made the most of his opportunities thus far, logging 21 carries for 90 yards through his first two games. The 49ers are favored in Sunday's matchup and the Cardinals' defense is spotty, allowing 243 rushing yards over two games. An early advantage, especially on the ground, could lead San Francisco to ease off star RB Christian McCaffrey and give Black more opportunities. The Indiana product still doesn't play enough to be viable in redraft fantasy leagues, but has become a valuable stash in deeper formats.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black gets seven carries in Week 2
metadata.description: Kaelon Black gained 25 yards on seven carries in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
metadata.analysis: After gaining 65 yards on 14 carries in Week 1, Black saw his attempts cut in half in Week 2. The 49ers' rushing attack was not very efficient in Sunday's win, but Brock Purdy more than made up for that with his passing prowess. Black has gained 90 yards on 21 carries through two games, and he maintains decent fantasy value as the backup to Christian McCaffrey.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black - Seven touches to CMC's 14
metadata.description: Black (groin) rushed seven times for 25 yards and wasn't targeted in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
metadata.analysis: Black suited up for his second NFL contest after being listed as questionable coming into the game. He actually had two more rushing yards than Christian McCaffrey, but McCaffrey scored two touchdowns on 10 carries and added four catches for 43 yards. Black is poised to continue splitting the rushing workload with CMC in Week 3 against the Cardinals, though McCaffrey remains the preferred option in valuable goal-line and passing situations.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black (groin) active for Week 2
metadata.description: Kaelon Black (groin) is active for Week 2 for the San Francisco 49ers against the Miami Dolphins according to Nick Wagoner.
metadata.analysis: Black is good to go after not experiencing any setbacks during pregame warmups for head coach Kyle Shanahan, offering another dynamic option alongside Christian McCaffrey out of the San Francisco backfield against the Dolphins Sunday.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black - Active as expected Sunday
metadata.description: Black (groin) is active for Sunday's Week 2 matchup against the Dolphins, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: The rookie running back was reported to be trending up for Sunday's contest earlier Sunday, and his availability now has been made official. Black will therefore once again serve as the primary backup to Christian McCaffrey, a role that afforded the former 15 touches (14 carries, one reception) across 28 snaps in a Week 1 win over the Rams in Melbourne, Australia.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black Active Against Dolphins
metadata.description: San Francisco 49ers running back Kaelon Black (groin) is listed as active for Sunday's Week 2 battle against the visiting Miami Dolphins, the Athletic's Matt Barrows reported via the X platform. Black was limited in practice on Thursday and Friday after sustaining the injury mid-week, but didn't appear on the injury list ahead of Sunday's home opener. The rookie back out of Indiana had 14 carries for 65 yards against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 1, and he should have an even easier time getting the ball downfield against a Dolphins defense that allowed 130 rushing yards to the Las Vegas Raiders to open up the season. The 49ers will likely lean heavily on Christian McCaffrey once again, but Black should see a similar workload to Week 1 if his injury doesn't flare up mid-game.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black (groin) expected to play on Sunday
metadata.description: Kaelon Black (groin) is expected to play on Sunday against the Dolphins.
metadata.analysis: If Black plays it seems unlikely he'll have the 50-50 split with Christian McCaffrey he had last time out, and likely will play a more complementary role. However, if the Niners do get up big, he could see a decent amount of touches, so he could be flex-worthy in deep formats.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black - On track to play Sunday
metadata.description: Black (groin) is on track to play Sunday against the Dolphins, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
metadata.analysis: Black popped up on Thursday's injury report as a limited participant due to a groin injury, and he was given a questionable designation after getting in another limited session Friday. While there is reason to believe he will take the field Sunday, his availability will not be confirmed until the 49ers release their inactives 90 minutes before Sunday's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black Expected to Play Against Miami on Sunday
metadata.description: San Francisco 49ers running back Kaelon Black (groin) is expected to be active for Sunday's Week 2 contest against the Miami Dolphins, according to Adam Schefter of ESPN.com. He was listed as questionable after logging limited practice sessions on Thursday and Friday, but it appears that he'll be healthy enough to play this weekend. Black is coming off a very impressive NFL debut against the Los Angeles Rams during Week 1 in Australia. He took on a sizable role in the Niners' victory, rushing for 65 yards on 14 carries despite being listed second on the depth chart behind Christian McCaffrey. His astoundingly high volume could be the product of San Francisco jumping out to an early lead, but we'd expect a similar workload in Week 2 with the 49ers favored by 13.5 points over the Dolphins.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black is a Shaky Flex Play
metadata.description: San Francisco 49ers running back Kaelon Black (groin) is considered questionable ahead of the Week 2 matchup against the Miami Dolphins. Black was impressive during his NFL debut when he rushed for 65 yards on 14 attempts in the win over the Los Angeles Rams. It was surprising to see the rookie back see that many carries in the backfield, which led him to be a popular waiver wire pickup. Now, Black is uncertain to play on Sunday due to groin tightness. Even if he does play, Black will be a risky starting option given the fact that he probably won't be 100 percent healthy heading into this game. The 49ers might lean on Jordan James or wide receiver Deebo Samuel Sr. to relieve Christian McCaffrey in the backfield. Fantasy managers should consider Black a low-end flex option for this weekend.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black (groin) questionable to play Sunday
metadata.description: Kaelon Black (groin) is questionable to play in Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins.
metadata.analysis: The rookie was added to the injury report due to a groin issue on Thursday and will officially be questionable to play in Sunday's game against the Dolphins. He was quite involved in San Francisco's season opener last week, so his absence would likely lead to Christian McCaffrey seeing a supermajority of touches for the team in Week 2.
